sourceSeed: At Beacon Court, a night-shift renter who paid in full is locked out by a forged self-eviction; the former lover who can expose the false consent built its verification engine.

source.premise: At Beacon Court, a night-shift renter who paid in full is locked out by a forged self-eviction; the former lover who can expose the false consent built its verification engine.
boundaries: Original fiction: no living person's likeness, voice, biography, names or private records; original synthetic cast only after rights clearance
No Native story contribution or Indigenous cultural claim implied by this AI-origin market research; independently contributed stories remain another customer
The landlord and tenant system is invented speculative suspense, not real legal, tenant-rights or software guidance
A source reference, screen UI, market statistic or consumer prompt never authenticates a rent payment, verified consent or provider allocation
No video generations, paid orders or publication absent source-approved original character/location image bytes, model consent and independent receiving

market.audienceHypothesis: US mobile-first viewers who enjoy female-led romantic suspense, revenge/status reversal and recognizably precarious rent/work pressures; gender/age estimates are category-level, not a verified customer profile.
market.dramaticHypothesis: The payoff is Ada deciding to protect other tenants' privacy and compel voluntary testimony, instead of a one-dimensional revenge fantasy. Her former partner's technical complicity introduces slow-burn romantic suspense without rewarding coercion.

observations.finding: Q1 2026 short-drama app downloads surpassed 850M, with high-emotion romance, revenge, family conflict and status reversal identified as core genres; not evidence this specific property will sell.
ReelShort US daily mobile minutes per user exceeded several general streamers in Q4 2025; does not forecast episode retention for an original script.
The US genre has a substantial female audience aged approximately 25–55, with cliffhangers and TikTok/Shorts/Reels discovery; this is descriptive, not a required cast or audience restriction.
23% of US renters reported being behind on rent at some point during 2025; the fictional Ada is paid-up and faces alleged algorithmic false consent.

71% of surveyed US adults expect AI to lead to fewer jobs in the next two decades; the story uses credible anxieties about workplace and algorithmic power without representing a surveyed AI eviction incident.

preregisteredPilotTests.objective: Compare market-sourced emotional hooks after a legally qualified pilot exists; do not buy advertising without account and budget authority.
preregisteredPilotTests.teaserA: Paid in full. Locked out. The supposed eviction is in her own voice.
preregisteredPilotTests.teaserB: She trusted him. He built the system that evicted her.
preregisteredPilotTests.cadence: 72-second episodes with genuine 9:16 acting; free-to-finish original public pilot, no fake scarcity or app coin mechanics
outcomes: 3-second hold rate per exposure, by platform and teaser creative
30-second conditional retention and episode completion, denominators reported
Episode-one to episode-two voluntary continuation, not clicks equated with purchases
Qualitative independent reviews of motivation, performance, original voice/character identity and audience confusion
Accepted finished minutes and source-dimensioned full cost per accepted minute, never provider estimates treated as settled cash
preregisteredPilotTests.decisionRule: Prefer the teaser with higher properly denominated completion/continuation on an equal, recorded exposure cohort. Before adequate data, label result inconclusive rather than assigning invented thresholds or proclaiming a market gap.

preregisteredPilotTests.editRationale: The two 15-second A/B promos share the identical complete 8-second forged-voice cliffhanger and differ only in the first seven seconds (rent denial versus former-partner betrayal). This isolates which opening emotional hook attracts attention; 7-second first clips retain nearly all spoken dialogue. Both EDLs reuse source footage instead of demanding extra provider generations.

series.tagline: She paid the rent. The building forged her goodbye.
series.set: Beacon Court, a deliberately fictional 2032 apartment building; all first-three-episode dramatic beats share a single modest glass lobby and interior access door.

visualBible.frame: 9:16 portrait, 30fps compiled source, each shot 8s; original cinematic acting, recognizable identity and camera depth, NOT SVG animatics
visualBible.continuity: Ada: dark navy nightshift work jacket, damp shoulder seams, cloth shift badge; Ivo: pale gray maintenance coat and scar above right eyebrow; Corin: emerald blazer, small silver pin; lobby: teal-green access-reader LED against amber morning light; keep geography constant.
visualBible.lighting: Cold fluorescent institutional overhead, truthful wet daylight through lobby glass, reflections used sparingly; no synth film grain, no fake documentary logos.
visualBible.temporalSpace: Events unfold in continuous dawn lobby time. No unexplained costumes, door geometry or scene teleportation.
visualBible.textsAndScreens: All fictional rent notices, times, private data and tenant-response counts are editor-authored overlays inserted onto real blank screen plates, NOT hallucinated text inside provider shots.
visualBible.audio: Original licensed synthetic voices, room-tone, elevator hum, keycard denial and rain. Each shot requires genuine dialogue timing, acting and auditionable sound. No real person voice cloning.
visualBible.authorization: No images, performer voice IDs or location reference is admitted at this phase. Original AI fictional writing is a production proposal only.

episodes.title: Paid in Full
episodes.openingHook: She paid her rent. Her apartment locked her out anyway.

beats.action: Ada's door denies access despite a cleared rent payment
beats.consequence: She demands a person, not an automated denial

beats.action: Ada spots the inconsistent timestamps behind the lockout
beats.consequence: The manager fears the audit trail and summons the auditor

beats.action: Ada's former partner reveals a verified self-eviction authorized with her voice
beats.consequence: Ada can no longer trust the building's evidence or the one person who understands it
beats.question: Who used Ada's voice to approve an eviction she never requested?

shots.action: Ada in a rain-damp dark blue work jacket tries her building fob twice. Red light. Her shift bag lands heavily on the tile. Her private phone says payment cleared, but the physical door will not open.
shots.camera: Vertical tight two-plane shot: her expressive exhausted face in top half, fob and red door reader lower half; slow handheld push, no readable AI-generated phone text.

dialogue.text: I paid yesterday. Why won't the door open?

shots.editorialNotes: Post-edit UI insert: PAYMENT CLEARED / DOOR ACCESS DENIED. One fob click, one sharp denial chirp.

shots.action: Corin steps into the lobby from behind the glass concierge desk with a manila folder, composed and practiced. She positions herself between Ada and the locked interior door.
shots.camera: Over-shoulder to cold single on Corin; 85mm-like compressed vertical framing, controlled fluorescent ceiling and morning spill; no pan away from acting.

dialogue.text: Unit four-seventeen is in default. Clear the lobby.

shots.editorialNotes: Corin wears one distinctive dark emerald blazer and silver pin throughout the serial.

shots.action: Ada holds up a paper bank receipt with trembling hands, then steadies it against her battered work badge. She refuses to cry in front of the manager.
shots.camera: Close on fingers and paper edge with real human acting, tilt to eyes; do NOT synthesize legible bank text inside model frames.

dialogue.text: My bank cleared it. I can prove it.

shots.editorialNotes: Compositing: actual narrative-safe fictional receipt ID TX-2041, no real account number.

shots.action: Ada steps toward Corin with the receipt. Corin refuses eye contact and turns the folder so Ada cannot see its contents.
shots.camera: Tense vertical two-shot, shallow depth of field with both faces readable; single lobby window anchors continuity.

dialogue.text: Your payment reached a different account. That's not my problem.

shots.editorialNotes: Staging keeps both performers at natural physical distance; no slap or supernatural interface.

shots.action: Ada compares the receipt timestamp against her saved lockout notification. A calculation lands: the building had chosen to remove her before the deadline.
shots.camera: Tight face-to-phone rack focus; hold on the change from panic to forensic certainty; 9:16 legible eye movement.

dialogue.text: You ordered the lockout before my rent was due.

shots.editorialNotes: Edit overlay, NOT generative typography: LOCKOUT AUTHORIZED 23:41 / RENT DUE 00:00.

shots.action: For the first time Corin's calm fractures. She closes the folder too quickly and reaches for a private earpiece.
shots.camera: Still close-up, small involuntary blink reveals fear; foreground Ada is only an unfocused shoulder if visible.

dialogue.text: File your dispute on Monday. I'm done talking.

shots.editorialNotes: Legal process is fictional; this is not a claim that a real landlord can legally evict without process.

shots.action: Ivo, a former intimate partner in a pale gray maintenance coat, steps out of the service elevator. He recognizes Ada and freezes. Ada holds the bank paper between them.
shots.camera: Two-shot moving vertically from Ada's raised paper to Ivo's guilty eyes; shared lobby axis for later reverse angle.

dialogue.text: Ivo? You work for her now?
Don't sign anything.

shots.editorialNotes: Quiet elevator hum under an unfinished emotional recognition; recurring coat and scar on Ivo's eyebrow.

shots.action: Corin orders Ivo toward a security tablet. He looks at her, then silently chooses to face Ada instead, making his loyalty visibly uncertain.
shots.camera: Over-shoulder from Corin onto Ivo, natural hand and tablet movement, restrained rather than melodramatic crowd staging.

dialogue.text: Ivo. Show her the release.
Corin. Please.

shots.editorialNotes: The word RELEASE refers to a fictional automated building-account workflow, not a legal eviction judgment.

shots.action: Ivo turns the tablet toward Ada but she watches his face, not the screen. Her eyes widen when he reveals that the system contains a voice confirmation she never gave. Cut on her horrified refusal.
shots.camera: Extreme tight alternating vertical framing, last 1.5 seconds on Ada's face; add the fictional voice-record waveform in editorial only.

dialogue.text: It says you asked to leave. In your own voice.
I never said that.

shots.editorialNotes: Episode ends HARD on Ada's gaze and an ominous waveform audio cue. No real voice clone is authorized by this draft.

episodes.intendedDistribution: 720p+ vertical Shorts/Reels/TikTok if publisher later receives exact source and disclosure

episodes.title: The Verification
episodes.openingHook: The eviction has her voice. The timestamps have a different story.

beats.action: Ada contests the recording with evidence from her night shift
beats.consequence: Ivo inspects the machine's hidden audit trail

beats.action: Ivo finds a pattern of coerced or fabricated approvals
beats.consequence: Their old relationship becomes a source of leverage and mistrust

beats.action: Ivo confesses that he authored the consent-verification software
beats.consequence: Ada's only technical ally may be responsible for harming dozens of tenants
beats.question: Can Ada expose the forgeries without relying on their creator?

shots.action: Without leaving the same lobby, Ada peels back her hospital linen-work ID beside the tablet clock, physically planting her evidence before she speaks.
shots.camera: Close to medium; exhausted hands, fluorescent spill, a defensive breath; remain anchored on Ada.

dialogue.text: At two-thirteen? I was on the hospital night shift.

shots.editorialNotes: No real hospital, patient or employer identities.

shots.action: Ivo listens to the playback through a private earpiece and flinches on one unnatural syllable. He is shaken by the resemblance.
shots.camera: Vertical close-up on Ivo's small human reaction, tablet audio low and distorted; no photoreal deepfake of a real person.

dialogue.text: Then why does the system have your voice?

shots.editorialNotes: The supposed voice forgery is fictional; any produced audio requires original fictional performer's licensed voice.

shots.action: Corin taps a glossy compliance badge and passes the lobby door as if an appeal would be a personal insult.
shots.camera: Confident single, high-key lobby cool lighting; shoulder and badge silhouette not legible text.

dialogue.text: It's verified consent. There is nothing left to discuss.

shots.editorialNotes: Corin asserts rather than proves verification.

shots.action: Ada points to the original notification order on Ivo's tablet. Ivo watches the two timestamps finally make sense.
shots.camera: Tight equal-status two-shot, slow push into shared tablet silhouette, return to synchronized expressions.

dialogue.text: The lockout happened before the approval. Look.

shots.editorialNotes: Editor inserts original fictional sequential event stamps; never claim actual provider receipt.

shots.action: Ivo swipes past the decorative interface into a plain audit page; his confidence fades as he sees a repeating pattern.
shots.camera: Vertical close on Ivo eyes and hand; actual words added as source-owned editor overlay.

dialogue.text: There's a second log. The residents never see it.

shots.editorialNotes: Reveal only pseudonymous fictional event IDs in editorial.

shots.action: Ada lowers her voice while keeping her body between Corin and Ivo, deliberately giving him space to choose.
shots.camera: Ada in half shadow by the locked door, no heroic pose, measured resolve.

dialogue.text: Can you open it, or are you protecting her?

shots.editorialNotes: Emotion: loyalty test rather than data exposition.

shots.action: Ivo scrolls through an internal count without showing private names. A visible wince: many tenants are affected.
shots.camera: Locked-in close-up; an empty strip of tablet glass catches Ada's reflection.

dialogue.text: Forty-two move-outs. The same fake consent pattern.

shots.editorialNotes: Editor shows count 42 only, no fictional tenants' identifying information.

shots.action: Corin is back in the doorway and hears him. Ivo makes a decision not to hide the tablet, even when she takes one step toward it.
shots.camera: Tense two-person profile composition, ambient door latch snapping shut.

dialogue.text: Ivo. Think carefully about what you're saying.

shots.editorialNotes: No property manager's claim should be presented as lawful disclosure policy.

shots.action: Ada stares at Ivo, not at the screen. His face drops; he can no longer conceal his connection to the forgery. Finish on Ada's recognition of betrayal.
shots.camera: Tight 9:16 reverse angle with the same physical door and coat from episode one; hold ending reaction, not text.

dialogue.text: How do you know its blind spots?
Because I built the verification engine.

shots.editorialNotes: Cliffhanger is emotional complicity, not a claim about real-world AI verification products.

episodes.intendedDistribution: 720p+ vertical Shorts/Reels/TikTok if publisher later receives exact source and disclosure

episodes.title: The Forty-Third Door
episodes.openingHook: The one person who can prove her innocence helped build the system.

beats.action: Ada demands Ivo's accountability before accepting his help
beats.consequence: They separate lawful evidence and original tenants' permission from technical access

beats.action: Ada begins organizing voluntary tenant corroboration despite Corin's interference
beats.consequence: The contested machine evidence becomes testimony from people, not another automated verdict

beats.action: Corin's own family appears as the last victim of the manipulated system
beats.consequence: The apparent antagonist has a personal stake and an undisclosed source of control
beats.question: Why is Corin's mother the forty-third person targeted by the system?

shots.action: Ada stands very still opposite Ivo. He reaches for her hand but she steps back; refusal without melodramatic physical violence.
shots.camera: Portrait two-shot, quiet concrete wall and locked lobby in background, lips readable.

dialogue.text: You built a machine that signed for strangers?
I built the verification. Corin changed the rule.

shots.editorialNotes: No claim of known real software exploit; the invented system exists only in this fiction.

shots.action: Corin tries to seize Ivo's tablet. Ada gently intercepts without touching Corin, keeping a practical ethical distance.
shots.camera: Stabilized chest-up two-shot, private tenant names never visible in-camera.

dialogue.text: That's private tenant data.
Then we ask the tenants themselves.

shots.editorialNotes: Privacy is the dramatic choice: original residents consent rather than being exposed.

shots.action: Ivo opens the resident-facing dispute page rather than the administrator archive. He turns off his privileged view.
shots.camera: Single on Ivo, slow rack-focus away from screen toward his guilty face.

dialogue.text: They can choose to attest. No stolen records.

shots.editorialNotes: Do not represent this as a real legally compliant attestation system.

shots.action: Ada takes blank consent cards from the concierge counter and folds them. She points toward mailboxes, deciding to do the slow work.
shots.camera: Medium vertical: cards in hands foreground and Ada's determined face behind.

dialogue.text: Forty-two doors. Forty-two people get to choose.

shots.editorialNotes: Cards are fictional consent invitations, not actual privacy forms.

shots.action: Corin raises Ivo's revoked access tag. Ivo glances once and refuses to reach for her offered escape.
shots.camera: Compressed close two-shot, red tag reflected on glass, no extra cast.

dialogue.text: Your access is revoked. You can't help her.

shots.editorialNotes: Manager is threatening, not performing a valid user-account revocation verified by a real API.

shots.action: Ivo puts down his privileged tablet and places an unmarked tenant instruction card on the counter instead.
shots.camera: Close on hands and honest eye line, compassionate original performance.

dialogue.text: She doesn't need my password. She needs witnesses.

shots.editorialNotes: Customer sign-off and data rights remain separate real-world production holds.

shots.action: Ada watches the fictional first consent reply appear on her phone. Relief flashes, followed by alarm as the reply count rapidly rises.
shots.camera: Vertical shoulder to face, notifications added through deterministic editorial overlays only.

dialogue.text: One answer. Then five. They're all seeing it.

shots.editorialNotes: This is fictional neighbor testimony, not fabricated market research.

shots.action: Corin stares at the exact count 43 on a private paper list and loses her practiced composure for the first time.
shots.camera: Extreme close on Corin's trembling hand gripping paper, cut to wet eyes; no magic UI.

dialogue.text: Forty-three. There weren't supposed to be forty-three.

shots.editorialNotes: Use original silver pin as continuous wardrobe marker.

shots.action: Ada confronts Corin as Corin cannot tear her eyes away from a family photo she has hidden in the folder. Corin speaks in a near-whisper.
shots.camera: Tense close vertical two-shot with photo edge, no third performed face; hold 1s on Ada's moral complication.

dialogue.text: Who is the forty-third?
My mother.

shots.editorialNotes: Episode cliffhanger complicates the antagonist; never need to synthesize the mother's face in this season.

episodes.intendedDistribution: 720p+ vertical Shorts/Reels/TikTok if publisher later receives exact source and disclosure
